prompt: A prism splits white sunlight into a rainbow spectrum, with violet light bent more than red light. Why is violet bent more?

options.text: Violet light travels fastest through glass, so it deflects most
The prism absorbs red light and lets violet pass straight
Violet light is heavier than red light and is pulled down more
Glass refracts shorter wavelengths more strongly than longer wavelengths, and violet has a shorter wavelength than red

explanation: Refractive index depends slightly on wavelength — dispersion. Shorter wavelengths such as violet are slowed and bent more in glass than longer wavelengths such as red, so white light fans out into a spectrum.
